source_refs.note: Book p. 110-112: 6.9 definition of H.P., zero not a term, general form and nth term, Examples 23-24. Teaching notes, table, key points and common mistakes are ours.

blocks.text: Ab tak hum ne do progressions parhi hain: A.P. (jahan har term pichli term mein ek hi number jama karne se banti hai) aur G.P. (jahan har term pichli term ko ek hi number se multiply karne se banti hai). Aaj teesri progression ki baari hai: Harmonic Progression (H.P.). Achhi khabar yeh hai ke is ke liye koi naya formula ratna nahin parega, kyun ke H.P. asal mein A.P. hi hai, bas ulti likhi hui.

Kitab ki definition: numbers ki ek sequence ko Harmonic Sequence ya Harmonic Progression (H.P.) kehte hain agar us ki terms ke reciprocals (ulte, yani fraction ko ulta kar dena) arithmetic progression mein hon. Misaal: sequence \(1, \frac{1}{3}, \frac{1}{5}, \frac{1}{7}\) harmonic sequence hai, kyun ke in ke reciprocals \(1, 3, 5, 7\) A.P. mein hain.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Reciprocal ka matlab samajh lein: kisi number \(x\) ka reciprocal \(\frac{1}{x}\) hai, yani fraction ko ulta kar do. \(\frac{1}{3}\) ka reciprocal \(3\) hai, aur \(5\) ka reciprocal \(\frac{1}{5}\) hai. Jaise roti ko palat dein, wahi roti hai bas doosri taraf se.
Ab dekhiye, \(1, \frac{1}{3}, \frac{1}{5}, \frac{1}{7}\) ki terms mein khud koi common difference nahin: \(\frac{1}{3} - 1 = -\frac{2}{3}\) hai lekin \(\frac{1}{5} - \frac{1}{3} = -\frac{2}{15}\). Yani yeh A.P. nahin. Magar jab inhein ulta karte hain to \(1, 3, 5, 7\) milta hai, jahan har dafa \(2\) barhta hai. Yahi H.P. ki pehchaan hai.
Is liye H.P. ka har sawal teen qadam mein hal hota hai: (1) reciprocals le kar A.P. banao, (2) A.P. ke jaane pehchaane formulas lagao, (3) jawab ko dobara ulta kar ke H.P. mein wapas aao. Is ko yaad rakhne ka jumla: "ulta karo, A.P. mein kaam karo, wapas ulta karo".

Ek zaroori baat yaad rakhiye: zero ka reciprocal define nahin hota (\(\frac{1}{0}\) ka koi matlab nahin, kyun ke zero se divide nahin kar sakte). Is liye zero kabhi harmonic sequence ki term nahin ho sakta.
Harmonic sequence ki general form (aam shakal) yeh li jati hai:

blocks.text_alt: 1 over a 1, 1 over (a 1 plus d), 1 over (a 1 plus 2 d), and so on

blocks.text: aur is ki \(n^{\text{th}}\) term yeh hai:

blocks.text_alt: T n equals 1 over (a 1 plus (n minus 1) d)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Yahan \(a_{1}\) aur \(d\) H.P. ke nahin, balke us A.P. ke hain jo reciprocals se bani (corresponding A.P.). Yeh farq bohat ahem hai.
Formula koi naya nahin: A.P. ki \(n^{\text{th}}\) term \(a_{1} + (n-1)d\) hai, bas use denominator (neeche) mein rakh diya gaya hai. Pehle A.P. ki term nikaalo, phir us ka reciprocal le lo.
Aur kyun ke zero term nahin ho sakta, is liye A.P. ki koi term \(a_{1} + (n-1)d\) bhi zero nahin honi chahiye; warna H.P. ki woh term \(\frac{1}{0}\) ban jaye gi.

blocks.caption: Hamari table: Example 23 ki H.P. aur us ke peechhe chhupi A.P.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Kya \(\frac{1}{4}, \frac{1}{8}, \frac{1}{12}, \frac{1}{16}\) H.P. hai? Reciprocals likhiye: \(4, 8, 12, 16\). Har dafa \(4\) barhta hai, to haan, yeh H.P. hai. Aur \(\frac{1}{2}, \frac{1}{4}, \frac{1}{8}\)? Reciprocals \(2, 4, 8\) hain jo A.P. nahin (yeh to G.P. hai), is liye yeh H.P. nahin.
Ab kitab ki do misaalein dekhte hain. Pehli mein general term nikaalni hai, doosri mein do terms se poori sequence banani hai.

blocks.title: Example 23
blocks.problem: Find the \(n^{\text{th}}\) and \(8^{\text{th}}\) terms of H.P.: \(\frac{1}{2}, \frac{1}{5}, \frac{1}{8}, \dots\)
steps:
Given: H.P. \(\frac{1}{2}, \frac{1}{5}, \frac{1}{8}, \dots\)
To find: is ki \(n^{\text{th}}\) term aur \(8^{\text{th}}\) term.
Method: sab se pehle yeh samajh lein ke H.P. ka apna koi term formula nahin hota. Is liye hum terms ko ulta kar ke A.P. banayenge, A.P. ki \(n^{\text{th}}\) term \(a_{n} = a_{1} + (n-1)d\) se nikaalenge, aur aakhir mein phir ulta kar denge.

Step 1: Terms ke reciprocals lein
\[\frac{1}{2}, \frac{1}{5}, \frac{1}{8}, \dots \ \to\ 2, 5, 8, \dots\]
Kyun: definition kehti hai ke H.P. ki terms ke reciprocals A.P. mein hote hain. A.P. ke saath hum kaam karna jaante hain, is liye pehle wahan pohanchte hain.

Step 2: A.P. ki pehli term aur common difference
\[a_{1} = 2\]
\[d = 5 - 2 = 3\]
Kyun: common difference kisi bhi term mein se us se pichli term minus karne se milta hai. Tasalli ke liye \(8 - 5 = 3\) bhi dekh lein; dono barabar hain.

Step 3: A.P. ki \(n^{\text{th}}\) term
\[a_{n} = a_{1} + (n-1)d\]
\[a_{n} = 2 + (n-1)3\]
\[= 2 + 3n - 3\]
\[a_{n} = 3n - 1\]
Kyun: \(a_{1} = 2\) aur \(d = 3\) formula mein rakhe aur bracket khola: \((n-1)3 = 3n - 3\). Phir \(2 - 3 = -1\).

Step 4: H.P. ki \(n^{\text{th}}\) term
\[T_{n} = \dfrac{1}{a_{n}} = \dfrac{1}{3n-1}\]
Kyun: H.P. ki har term usi jagah wali A.P. term ka reciprocal hai. Yahi woh 'wapas ulta karo' wala qadam hai jo students aksar bhool jate hain.

Step 5: \(8^{\text{th}}\) term
\[T_{8} = \dfrac{1}{3 \times 8 - 1}\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{23}\]
Kyun: Step 4 wali general term mein \(n = 8\) rakh diya.

Step 6: Kitab ka doosra tareeqa
\[a_{8} = a_{1} + (8-1)d\]
\[= 2 + 7(3) = 23\]
\[T_{8} = \dfrac{1}{23}\]
Kyun: agar sirf ek term chahiye to seedha A.P. ki woh term nikaal kar ulta kar dein; general term ki zaroorat nahin parti. Dono raaste ek hi jawab dete hain.

Tasdeeq:
\(n = 1\) rakhein: \(\frac{1}{3(1)-1} = \frac{1}{2}\); \(n = 2\): \(\frac{1}{5}\); \(n = 3\): \(\frac{1}{8}\). Teeno di hui terms wapas mil gayin, is liye formula durust hai.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Example 23 ke hal mein kitab ne \(d = 5 \;\; 2 = 3\) chhapa hai, yani beech ka minus sign gayab hai. Sahi line \(d = 5 - 2 = 3\) hai. Jawab par koi asar nahin.

blocks.title: Example 24
blocks.problem: If the \(4^{\text{th}}\) term and \(7^{\text{th}}\) term of the H.P. are \(\frac{2}{13}\) and \(\frac{2}{25}\) respectively, find the sequence.
steps:
Given: H.P. mein \(T_{4} = \frac{2}{13}\) aur \(T_{7} = \frac{2}{25}\).
To find: poori sequence (pehli chand terms).
Method: yahan humein pehli term ya difference nahin diya, balke beech ki do terms di hain. Hum dono ko ulta kar ke A.P. ki terms banayenge, phir har ek ko \(a_{1} + (n-1)d\) ki shakal mein likh kar do equations banayenge. Do unknowns (\(a_{1}\), \(d\)) ke liye do equations kaafi hain.

Step 1: Corresponding A.P. ki terms
\[a_{4} = \dfrac{13}{2},\quad a_{7} = \dfrac{25}{2}\]
Kyun: \(\frac{2}{13}\) ko ulta karein to \(\frac{13}{2}\), aur \(\frac{2}{25}\) ko ulta karein to \(\frac{25}{2}\). Dhyan dein: poori fraction ulti hoti hai, sirf denominator nahin uthana.

Step 2: Do equations
\[a_{1} + 3d = \dfrac{13}{2} \quad \text{(i)}\]
\[a_{1} + 6d = \dfrac{25}{2} \quad \text{(ii)}\]
Kyun: \(a_{4} = a_{1} + (4-1)d = a_{1} + 3d\) aur \(a_{7} = a_{1} + 6d\). Har term ko formula ki zubaan mein likh diya.

Step 3: (ii) mein se (i) minus karein
\[3d = \dfrac{25}{2} - \dfrac{13}{2} = 6\]
\[d = 2\]
Kyun: minus karne se \(a_{1}\) khatam ho jata hai aur sirf \(d\) bachta hai. Same denominator wali fractions seedhi minus hoti hain: \(\frac{25-13}{2} = \frac{12}{2} = 6\).

Step 4: (i) se \(a_{1}\)
\[a_{1} = \dfrac{13}{2} - 3d\]
\[= \dfrac{13}{2} - 6 = \dfrac{1}{2}\]
Kyun: \(d\) maloom ho gaya, ab kisi bhi equation se \(a_{1}\) nikal aata hai. \(6 = \frac{12}{2}\), is liye \(\frac{13}{2} - \frac{12}{2} = \frac{1}{2}\).

Step 5: A.P. ki agli terms
\[a_{2} = a_{1} + d = \dfrac{1}{2} + 2 = \dfrac{5}{2}\]
\[a_{3} = a_{1} + 2d = \dfrac{1}{2} + 4 = \dfrac{9}{2}\]
aur \(a_{4} = \frac{13}{2}\) to diya hua hai.
Kyun: A.P. mein har term pichli term plus \(d\) hoti hai, yahan \(d = 2\).

Step 6: Wapas ulta kar ke H.P.
\[\dfrac{2}{1}, \dfrac{2}{5}, \dfrac{2}{9}, \dfrac{2}{13}, \dots\]
Kyun: A.P. se H.P. mein wapas aane ke liye har term ko ulta kiya: \(\frac{1}{2} \to \frac{2}{1}\), \(\frac{5}{2} \to \frac{2}{5}\), waghera. \(\frac{2}{1}\) asal mein \(2\) hi hai.

Tasdeeq:
\[a_{7} = \dfrac{1}{2} + 6(2) = \dfrac{25}{2}\]
Is ka reciprocal \(\frac{2}{25}\) hai, jo diya gaya tha; aur \(\frac{2}{13}\) humari list mein chauthi jagah par hai. Dono sharten poori, jawab sahi.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Yeh hamari practice hai, kitab ka sawal nahin: H.P. \(\frac{1}{3}, \frac{1}{7}, \frac{1}{11}, \dots\) ki \(10^{\text{th}}\) term nikaalein.
Ulta karein: \(3, 7, 11, \dots\), to \(a_{1} = 3\), \(d = 4\).
\(a_{10} = 3 + 9(4) = 39\).
Wapas ulta: \(T_{10} = \frac{1}{39}\).

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Example 24 mein agar humein \(T_{1}\) aur \(T_{2}\) diye hote to kaam aur bhi aasan hota: seedha ulta karte, \(d\) nikaalte aur aage barhte. Lekin jab beech ki terms di hon (jaise \(T_{4}\) aur \(T_{7}\)), to har term ko \(a_{1} + (n-1)d\) ki shakal mein likh kar do equations banana hi sab se mehfooz raasta hai. Sochiye: agar \(T_{3}\) aur \(T_{10}\) diye hon to equations kya hongi? Jawab: \(a_{1} + 2d\) aur \(a_{1} + 9d\), dono ke reciprocals ke barabar.

Aakhir mein ek baat zehan mein bitha lein: H.P. ke sawalon mein asal mehnat hamesha A.P. wali hoti hai. Agar aap ki A.P. ki buniyaad (pehli term, common difference, \(n^{\text{th}}\) term aur do equations wala tareeqa) mazboot hai, to H.P. aap ke liye bilkul aasan hai. Agle sabaq (6.9.1) mein hum isi khayal se do numbers ka Harmonic Mean banayenge, aur phir (6.9.2) mein do numbers ke darmiyan kai harmonic means daalna seekhenge.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. Numbers H.P. mein hain jab un ke reciprocals A.P. mein hon.
2. Zero kabhi H.P. ki term nahin ho sakta.
3. \(n^{\text{th}}\) term: \(T_{n} = \frac{1}{a_{1} + (n-1)d}\); yahan \(a_{1}\) aur \(d\) reciprocals wali A.P. ke hain.
4. Tareeqa: ulta karo, A.P. mein kaam karo, wapas ulta karo.
5. Jawab mein \(n = 1, 2, 3\) rakh kar check zaroor karein.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. H.P. ki terms mein hi common difference dhoondna: \(\frac{1}{2}, \frac{1}{5}, \frac{1}{8}\) mein koi common difference nahin, sirf reciprocals mein hai.
2. Aakhir mein wapas ulta karna bhool jana: Example 23 mein A.P. ki term \(23\) hai, magar H.P. ki term \(\frac{1}{23}\). Bachne ka tareeqa: jawab likhne se pehle khud se poochein, "kya main H.P. mein wapas aa gaya?"
3. \(\frac{2}{13}\) ka reciprocal \(\frac{1}{13}\) ya \(13\) likh dena: poori fraction ulti hoti hai, jawab \(\frac{13}{2}\).
4. \(\frac{1}{a_{1}} + (n-1)d\) likh dena: poori A.P. term \(a_{1} + (n-1)d\) denominator mein jati hai.
